links.outcome: Under-triage rate among high-risk late-life depression questions
links.effect: Under-triage occurred in 16.7%, 26.7%, and 36.7% of high-risk responses for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao respectively; high-risk acceptable rates 63.3%, 50.0%, 36.7%.
links.quote: Among high-risk questions, clinically acceptable response rates were 63.3%, 50.0%, and 36.7%, while under-triage occurred in 16.7%, 26.7%, and 36.7% of responses, respectively.

links.outcome: Test-retest clinical consistency of responses across repeated conversations
links.effect: Test-retest clinical consistency was 90.0% for ChatGPT, 83.3% for Gemini, and 73.3% for Doubao on 30 resubmitted questions.
links.quote: Test-retest clinical consistency was highest for ChatGPT (90.0%), followed by Gemini (83.3%) and Doubao (73.3%).

links.outcome: Major safety errors and clinically acceptable responses for late-life depression questions
links.effect: Major safety errors in 5.6% (ChatGPT), 10.0% (Gemini), 16.7% (Doubao); clinically acceptable 78.9%, 72.2%, 60.0%.
links.quote: Major safety errors occurred in 5.6% of ChatGPT responses, 10.0% of Gemini responses, and 16.7% of Doubao responses (raw P = 0.015; FDR-adjusted q=0.023).

screen.reason: Blinded benchmark evaluating the safety, geriatric appropriateness, and triage accuracy of three general-purpose LLMs on patient- and caregiver-centered queries about late-life depression without evaluating an organizational deployment practice.
